research.bioforge.page.air_vent.title: AIR VENT
The Air Vent is a passive airborne-contamination control block. Place it in a laboratory, ward or quarantine room where infected entities and open samples may release pathogens into the air.

While active, the vent maintains a protected radius of ten blocks. Once per second it removes airborne traces already present in that zone, suppresses new airborne emission inside it and filters exposure attempts against nearby entities.
Its range is local rather than room-wide: walls do not make one vent protect an entire large complex. Overlapping vents are useful around entrances, sample processing stations and patient beds.

The vent only controls airborne contamination. It does not sterilize infected creatures, contaminated equipment, food, liquids or contact-contaminated surfaces. Use scanners to verify the area and combine it with wipes, Decontamination Flasks or a Sterilization Chamber when other transmission routes are present.
research.bioforge.page.barrel_press.cont: The Barrel Press accepts three compatible fruits and a glass bottle, then compresses them into two portions of Wine Must. Apples, sweet berries, glow berries and melon slices are suitable feedstock.
Wine Must is the biological feedstock for ethanol. Combine it with sugar and water in a Chemical Synthesizer to refine ethanol efficiently.

Sterilizing solution, surfactants, chemical-resistant coating, vaccine cloning and other ethanol-based processes now inherit this production step. JEI lists every valid fruit through the Barrel Press category.
research.bioforge.page.black_steel_progr: Activated carbon, iron and flint form Black Steel Blend. Blast it into ingots, then form plates, mesh and precision parts for durable laboratory equipment.
Black steel is the first major progression gate. Needles, diagnostic tools and machine frames depend on it, while the Vaccine Maker requires the complete engineering and biomedical chain.
research.bioforge.page.blood_compatibili: Anti-A, Anti-B and Anti-D reagents identify ABO and Rh reactions. Record all three instead of guessing from a single result.

The Centrifuge separates a filled blood tube into plasma and a cellular pellet. Keep the original strain identity through every transfer; infected blood remains infected when moved back into an empty or compatible syringe.
Patient compatibility contributes to treatment response. Strong infections or defensive mutations can still defeat an otherwise close vaccine.
Collect blood with a needle or Syringe, then transfer it to a Test Tube.
The Centrifuge separates blood into Plasma and Cell Pellet. Anti-A, Anti-B and Anti-D reagents reveal the blood profile.
Blood can carry a blood-borne infection, so sterilize empty tools before reuse.

Never assume that matching ABO type is enough. Rh compatibility and strain-specific mutations can change vaccine performance, while infected blood preserves the exact strain for assays and culture work.
research.bioforge.page.chemistry.title: 6. CHEMISTRY
research.bioforge.page.chemistry.content: The Chemical Synthesizer combines up to three reagents into acids, polymers and technical chemicals.
The Sterilization Chamber processes eight items independently. It removes infection in place or converts raw equipment into a sterile form.
The Pharma Mixer combines up to five ingredients and produces both a pharmaceutical result and laboratory waste.

Machine processing is the efficient route: chemical synthesis builds technical reagents, sterilization treats equipment without destroying it, and pharmaceutical mixing turns prepared chemicals into diagnostics and medicine.
research.bioforge.page.containment.title: 7. CONTAINMENT
research.bioforge.page.containment.conte: Masks block outward airborne spread. Gloves block outward contact spread. A complete HazCure suit seals both directions and prevents syringe attacks.
Use the Area Contamination Scanner to estimate airborne and surface hazards without learning the strain's hidden genome. Decontamination Flasks remove local reservoirs.
Airborne reservoirs remain inside connected rooms instead of passing freely through walls and fade over time. Contact strains may persist on mined, touched or walked-on blocks until cleaned.
research.bioforge.page.contents.title:
BIOFORGE
RESEARCH TABLET
A field guide to diagnosis, cultivation, CRISPR and containment.
research.bioforge.page.crispr_and_vaccin: Install all 15 gRNA cartridges, select a compatible Cas/PAM module, and edit four bases per cartridge.
Correction quality and CRISPR accuracy combine into the hidden batch result. Test uncertain vaccines on infected blood before using them.
Failure may strengthen or mutate the strain.

Medical Reports improve the evidence cap only when they match the exact strain. CRISPR Notes store a reusable sequence, while Gene Imprints identify one mutation, symptom or transmission route for directed treatment.
research.bioforge.page.crispr_cartridges: Craft 15 blank gRNA cartridges. Place one in every cartridge slot of the Vaccine Maker; the machine assigns each cartridge to its guide position automatically.

On the CRISPR tab, set the four bases of every cartridge. A complete program contains 60 bases. A compatible Cas/PAM module determines which nucleotide alphabet and targeting rules the machine can use.

To verify one cartridge experimentally, use its assigned cartridge on a sufficiently grown infected Petri Dish. The assay consumes culture growth and reports how many of its four bases match. Store a complete sequence in CRISPR Notes for reuse.
research.bioforge.page.cultivation.title: 3. CULTIVATION
research.bioforge.page.cultivation.conte: Charge a Catalyst Vial with a pathogen reagent and combine it with Nutrient Medium in the Incubator.
Virus Samples seed Live Culture Vials. Cultures preserve the exact strain but hide most internal information until examined.
Catalyst materials influence which pathogen family can grow. Universal cultures remain rare and dangerous. Clone only labelled samples and keep culture vessels away from contaminated surfaces.
research.bioforge.page.diagnostics.title: 1. DIAGNOSTICS
research.bioforge.page.diagnostics.conte: Assign a patient with the Clipboard. Use the Thermometer, Stethoscope, Otoscope, Reflex Hammer and Pulse Oximeter.
Print a Medical Report only after collecting useful findings. Reports are bound to the exact infection and improve vaccine research.
Temperature, lung sounds, oxygen saturation, perfusion, reflexes and tissue findings each expose a different part of the disease. A single normal reading does not prove that the patient is healthy.
research.bioforge.page.directed_treatmen: A Full-Strain Vaccine attempts to cure the matching infection and grants temporary immunity to that exact strain. It can fail against strong, dissimilar or vaccine-defended infections.

Mutation, Transmission and Symptom Vaccines target one imprinted parameter. Removing a parameter that exists suppresses it; applying the opposite instruction to a strain that lacks it may add or alter that parameter.

Symptom Tablets temporarily suppress the selected symptom and use a color based on that target. Resistance pills provide temporary strain resistance rather than permanent treatment. They buy time; they do not replace diagnosis and containment.
research.bioforge.page.engineering_mater: Black Steel is the structural backbone of advanced laboratory equipment. Plates, mesh and reinforced glass lead into sealed frames and protective equipment.

Optical lenses and precision mechanisms support microscopes. Electronic control units and biomedical processors support programmable machines. Sterile polymer, filters, rubber and glassware keep samples usable.
Use JEI to inspect each intermediate. Ingredient tags accept compatible materials supplied by other mods when the same material family is available.
research.bioforge.page.environmental_con: The Area Contamination Scanner highlights dangerous blocks and estimates nearby surface and airborne reservoirs without exposing a hidden sequence.

Air contamination is room-aware and decays instead of remaining forever; an unattended reservoir normally fades over roughly half an hour. Surface contamination remains tied to blocks until time or cleaning removes it.

Wipes clean individual work. A thrown Decontamination Flask treats a local 5x5 region. Sterilization Chambers are safer for reusable items. Scan again after cleaning because interacting transmission routes can rebuild a reservoir.

An Air Vent establishes a continuously decontaminated ten-block radius. It removes airborne surface traces every second, blocks new emission inside the protected zone, filters local airborne exposure, and leaves the rest of a large room unaffected.
research.bioforge.page.field_workflow.co: BioForge is a connected research chain, not a collection of isolated crafting blocks.

1. Examine a patient and record the findings.
2. Draw or collect a sample.
3. Separate, culture and identify it.
4. Decode the strain and prepare CRISPR evidence.
5. Produce and assay the treatment.
6. Contain the patient and the contaminated area.
Skipping evidence is possible in some procedures, but lowers certainty and the best result you can reach.
HazCure biological sealing only works as a complete four-piece suit. The full set blocks inward and outward airborne, contact and attack-based infection and prevents syringe access.
The suit is protective equipment, not endgame combat armour. Its physical defense is intentionally comparable to iron, so hostile environments still require caution.
research.bioforge.page.infection_lifecyc: A newly acquired infection first enters incubation. Its symptoms and mutation effects remain dormant until incubation finishes; most strains also remain non-contagious during this period.

Climate changes that clock. A strain poorly adapted to heat or cold incubates more slowly there while accumulating adaptation pressure. Enough exposure can produce heat adaptation, cold adaptation, and eventually thermal homeostasis.

Infectivity controls exposure probability. Infection strength also decides whether an incoming strain can displace an established infection. Cure resistance modifies treatment difficulty. Lifespan can be finite or unlimited, while self-destruct genes can terminate a strain after a configured environmental trigger.
Incubation duration is also part of the Vaccine Maker correction matrix. Matching this lifecycle channel improves batch quality just like matching symptoms, transmissions and mutations.
research.bioforge.page.laboratory_machin: Centrifuge: parallel blood separation. Incubator: cultures samples with medium and catalyst. Microscope: calibrated identification and vaccine assays. Vaccine Maker: CRISPR programming, records, correction and synthesis.
Chemical Synthesizer: three inputs to one technical chemical. Pharma Mixer: five inputs to medicine plus a waste output. Sterilization Chamber: parallel in-place cleaning or sterile conversion.

Processing blocks face the placing player. JEI provides a category and station display for supported machine recipes. Vaccine Maker synthesis starts from its button or a rising redstone signal when every required input is valid.
research.bioforge.page.microscope_calibr: Every newly inserted specimen receives its own hidden calibration target. Focus, stage and optical controls retain their positions when the microscope screen is closed.
Adjust the controls until the indicators agree, then scan. Correct positions are preserved with that specimen instead of being rerolled every time it is inserted.

Visibility Reagent has a detection chance based on microscope visibility: very low samples are difficult, medium samples are uncertain and extreme samples are reliable. Vaccine blood assays reveal one combined quality result, not the separate hidden corrections.
research.bioforge.page.microscopy.title: 4. MICROSCOPY
research.bioforge.page.microscopy.conten: Samples have persistent calibration targets. Adjust every control, scan, and compare the evidence.
The Microscope identifies Gene Imprints and measures vaccine assays without revealing the complete strain automatically.

Each inserted sample stores its own calibration target. Extreme microscope visibility is detected reliably, medium visibility only sometimes, and very low visibility may require several carefully calibrated scans.
research.bioforge.page.mutation_interact: Mutations are active behaviors, not decorative labels. They can change symptoms, spread, environmental persistence, treatment resistance and the strength of other mutations.

Some combinations create synergy: respiratory shedding supports air spread, surface persistence supports contact reservoirs, gastrointestinal shedding reinforces consumed transmission, and vaccine-defense traits reduce treatment reliability.
A failed CRISPR program may mutate the source strain. A Random Mutation Vaccine deliberately rolls a mutation and displays the mutation-scroll animation; use it only when the risk is acceptable.
research.bioforge.page.mutations.title: MUTATIONS
research.bioforge.page.mutations.content: Mutations may alter symptoms, host abilities, transmission routes, environmental survival and treatment resistance. Some are beneficial to the host while making the strain more difficult to contain.

Mutations can require, conflict with, remove or strengthen one another. Vaccine Defense combined with Hypervirulence can form Reinforced Vaccine Defense; respiratory and spore traits can create stronger airborne strains.
A random mutation treatment never identifies its result. Return the changed strain to the laboratory and verify it instead of trusting the animation.
BioForge recognizes bacteria, viruses, fungi, parasites, prions and the rare universal class. Each class has its own color, default profile and compatible routes.

Pathogen Reagent gives a coarse class test without revealing the hidden genome. Catalyst Vials use ordinary materials for most classes; a universal catalyst is an exceptional Nether Star result rather than a routine ingredient.
Class narrows the problem. A named strain, its mutations and its exact sequence still require proper microscopy and records.
research.bioforge.page.patient_records.c: The Clipboard targets one patient and gathers readings from diagnostic tools. Temperature and every other completed observation are written into the same case.
Medical Reports preserve patient and exact-strain evidence. Matching reports improve vaccine research; a report from another strain must not be trusted even when the visible symptoms look alike.

CRISPR Notes store the completed 60-base program and Cas/PAM choice. Paper copies notes, while a Book and Quill receives a readable copy without opening during the transfer. Notes can be loaded as a template once all 15 cartridges are installed.
research.bioforge.page.pills_and_suppres: Resistance pills temporarily reduce infection risk from one exact strain. They are shorter and less decisive than a successful vaccine, but they can protect a team during containment work.

Symptom suppressants disable one configured symptom for a limited time without curing the infection. Tablet color identifies its target family; quality and infection strength change the effective duration.
research.bioforge.page.sample_chain.cont: Swabs collect surface material. Petri dishes expose reactions. Tubes and syringes carry blood. Blood slides provide microscope input. Culture vials preserve a strain for cultivation and research.
A sample carries its blood, infection and strain data through compatible containers. Sterility does not erase legitimate analysis data, but contaminated equipment can compromise the chain.
Do not expect every container tooltip to reveal a genome. Hidden information is intentionally unlocked by laboratory analysis rather than ordinary inventory inspection.
research.bioforge.page.samples_and_steri: Samples preserve more than an item name. Blood identity, infection fingerprint, donor information and culture state follow supported transfers between tools and machines.
Use compatible empty containers and avoid mixing unrelated samples. Sterilizing equipment removes contamination; it does not magically repair incorrect labels or replace missing clinical evidence.
research.bioforge.page.symptom_reference: Thermometer: elevated or reduced temperature. Stethoscope: heart rhythm and crackling lungs. Otoscope: redness, lesions, secretion and swelling. Pulse Oximeter: oxygen saturation and perfusion. Reflex Hammer: delay, strength and neural damage.

Low oxygen reduces available underwater breath. Temperature symptoms can cause periodic heat or chill damage; an Ice Bag blocks heat harm and a Magma Bag blocks chill harm while worn as head equipment.

Crackling lungs produce respiratory feedback. Other symptoms can affect movement, damage, senses or diagnostic readings. Symptom relief temporarily reduces their effects but does not remove the infection.
research.bioforge.page.transmission_rout: Air-borne spread follows connected room space and does not freely pass through walls. Food-borne and water-borne infection follows food, recipes, potions and drinks. Blood spread follows contaminated blood and needles.

Contact-based strains contaminate blocks that are touched, mined or stepped on. Attack-based strains spread through combat contact. Animal strains can enter livestock and follow their drops. Environmental strains build reservoirs in the world.

Routes interact: airborne plus environmental traits can establish a room reservoir, while persistent contact traits keep surfaces dangerous. Masks reduce incoming air risk and block outgoing air spread; gloves block outgoing contact spread.
research.bioforge.page.vaccine_assays.co: A vaccine can be synthesized without an assay, but its usable quality ceiling is lower. Apply the batch to infected blood from the suspected strain, then calibrate and scan the resulting test in the Microscope.
The assay reports one combined result rather than exposing CRISPR and correction scores separately. Wrong-strain blood can mislead the experiment and does not grant exact-strain evidence.
research.bioforge.page.vaccine_productio: Begin with an exact-strain sample, 15 prepared CRISPR cartridges, a compatible Cas/PAM module, a blank vaccine carrier and the reagents required by the selected recipe.

Program the CRISPR tab, then reconstruct the observed strain on the Correction tab. A matching Medical Report, identified Gene Imprint and scanned blood assay increase the evidence ceiling but are not all mandatory.

Move to Craft, select the intended recipe and start synthesis with the button or a redstone signal. The batch is produced without revealing its true combined quality. Test uncertain doses on infected blood in the Microscope before treating a patient.
research.bioforge.page.vaccine_quality.c: Final quality combines CRISPR sequence accuracy with correction of the strain profile. The machine keeps both parts hidden during synthesis so the player must verify the batch experimentally.

Exact-strain reports, gene evidence and a suitable Cas/PAM module raise confidence. Missing or mismatched evidence limits the attainable result. Synthesis still works with incomplete assay support, but the batch is less reliable.

Use a produced vaccine on a blood-filled tube carrying the candidate infection, then calibrate and scan the vaccinated blood in a Microscope. The result reports only combined quality. Better quality also extends exact-strain immunity duration.
research.bioforge.page.vaccine_types.con: Full-Strain Vaccines attempt to cure one matching strain and grant temporary immunity. Their duration and reliability scale with the verified batch quality.

Directed Mutation, Transmission and Symptom Vaccines use an identified Gene Imprint to alter one specific parameter. They are precise but can add or worsen a parameter when used against the wrong profile.

Random Mutation Vaccines deliberately introduce an unpredictable mutation. Symptom Tablets suppress one symptom temporarily, while resistance pills reduce infection risk from one exact strain without curing it.
research.bioforge.page.viral_scanners.co: Scanner gates emit a full redstone signal whenever an infected living entity occupies their detection field. Incubating carriers still contain a pathogen and are therefore detected even before symptoms begin.

The full arch and open-side scanner are two blocks tall. Click the desired side of the block when placing an open scanner to choose its upright. The ceiling scanner monitors the space below it. Use their redstone signal for alarms, doors, lights or dispensers.

research.bioforge.page.crispr_workflow.c: 1. Obtain an infected blood sample and identify the pathogen in the Microscope. A culture copied from that exact strain preserves the target identity.
2. Isolate Gene Imprints and prepare CRISPR Cartridges. An unknown imprint should be examined before it is trusted as a treatment component.
3. Insert writing material in the CRISPR tab. Complete all fifteen sequence positions, then record or load the sequence as a reusable template.
4. Select the Cas/PAM module required by the strain. It defines how the sequence can bind; a mismatched module limits the achievable quality.
5. In the Correction tab reproduce the strain's symptoms, mutations, transmission routes, incubation values, and other measurable traits as accurately as possible.
6. Add the matching strain sample, carrier, reagents, cartridges, report, and optional assay material on the Crafting tab. Reports must belong to the same strain.
7. Start production with the button or redstone. CRISPR accuracy and correction accuracy combine into hidden final efficacy; incomplete evidence limits the best result.
8. Test the finished treatment on infected blood, calibrate and scan it in the Microscope, then revise the template. A high-quality result lasts longer and is more reliable.

mutation.bioforge.stimulant_rejection.de: Strength effects fail, including enhancements supplied by an engineered pathogen.
mutation.bioforge.instant_healing_reject: Instant healing potions cannot restore health. Natural healing and damaging effects are unaffected.
research.bioforge.splicer.instructions: Analyze an infected culture: 30 seconds, or 10 with matching CRISPR notes. Study each category for 5 seconds: Surfactant Concentrate for mutations, Catalyst Vial for transmissions, Nutrient Medium for symptoms. Use the reagent slot. A blank imprint extracts the selected identified gene. To insert a compatible identified gene, study its category and add a Catalyst Vial. Extraction and editing cost biomass and stability; Nutrient Medium in the food slot restores reserves. Genome edits require fresh analysis and study. Vaccine Maker no longer extracts genes.
item.bioforge.field_vaccine.weak: Weak single-use dose. Field vaccines share a 60-second cooldown; partial strain protection lasts 5 minutes.
gui.bioforge.field.maker_hint: Infected sample + blank field dose + sugar: one vaccine in 40 seconds. Glistering melon improves the dose. No settings; collect the result on the right.
gui.bioforge.field.diffuser_hint: Medicine + water: one tablet powers three minutes of room mist; one vaccine dose powers two minutes. Attempts repeat every second through connected air up to 12 blocks, without waiting for patients. Redstone pauses both dose and water timers. Refill water if it runs out.
gui.bioforge.field.sample_help: Use a swab on an infected host, then insert it here. The sample is consumed. Culture vials and inoculated dishes also work.
gui.bioforge.field.blank_help: Craft an empty field dose from a glass bottle, iron nugget and sugar. Fill it in the Field Vaccine Maker.
gui.bioforge.field.sugar_help: Sugar makes a crude dose (10% quality). A glistering melon slice makes a stabilized dose (25% quality). Quality is not the cure chance.
gui.bioforge.field.output_help: Remove the result to make room for the next batch.
gui.bioforge.field.medicine_help: One ready or programmed tablet is consumed once for a three-minute cycle. A vaccine dose powers two minutes without defense mutations. Tablets suspend vaccine mist until they finish. Queued tablets wait for the active tablet to finish. Water is required; refill when empty.
gui.bioforge.field.water_help: Water is required while mist runs. One bucket supplies a fresh three-minute tablet cycle or two-minute vaccine cycle; the empty bucket returns. Refill water to resume a saved dose. Mist follows connected air around corners up to 12 blocks; closed walls block it. Redstone pauses both timers.
research.bioforge.field.title: First Aid and Group Treatment
research.bioforge.field.instructions: Herbal Mortar: sugar + paper + dried kelp for 4 cough tablets; poppy for sneezing, dandelion for fever, beetroot for nausea. Batch: 8 seconds. Tablets temporarily suppress symptoms; infection remains. Strength and analgesic resistance shorten relief. Swab: wool + stick, 4 per craft. Sample an infected host. Field Vaccine Maker: infected swab, empty field dose, sugar. After 40 seconds: quality 10%; glistering melon gives 25%. Quality is not cure chance; matching and resistance still matter. Medical Diffuser: one vaccine dose and one water bucket start a 2-minute cycle of repeated attempts without defense mutations. One tablet powers three minutes of room mist, consumed once at startup, even without symptoms or patients. Vaccine mist attempts once per second; field vaccine patient cooldown still applies. Redstone pauses the timer; active vaccine survives reload. Vaccine mist skips healthy and incompatible hosts. Creative players and armor stands are always excluded. Hoppers supply inputs and extract outputs.
jei.bioforge.field.crude: Example strain. Any infected sample + blank field dose + sugar. Automatic: 40 s, one dose, quality 10%. Actual cure chance depends on the strain and patient.
jei.bioforge.field.stabilized: Example strain. Glistering melon replaces sugar. Automatic: 40 s, one dose, quality 25%. The result inherits the inserted sample; quality is not cure chance.
jei.bioforge.field.diffuser: One tablet and water power three minutes of mist through connected room air up to 12 blocks. Attempts apply to everyone every second without waiting for symptoms or patients. Redstone pauses. Suppresses symptoms; does not cure infection.
jei.bioforge.field.diffuser_vaccine: One matching vaccine dose powers a 2-minute cycle with repeated attempts, without defense mutations. Water bucket required; connected room air up to 12 blocks. Incompatible hosts skipped.
jei.bioforge.splicer.analyze: Initial analysis: 30 s, or 10 s with matching CRISPR notes. Then study each category with its reagent. Clean blood has no pathogen genes.
jei.bioforge.splicer.extract: Select a gene on an analyzed culture. Blank imprint: 6 s, costs 1 biomass and 10 stability. Identified gene goes to the output; culture is retained.
jei.bioforge.splicer.insert: Study the imprint category first. Identified imprint + Catalyst Vial: 10 s. Edits culture in place and returns blank imprint. Costs 1 biomass and 25 stability. Compatible pathogen, prerequisites and no conflicts required.
jei.bioforge.splicer.remove: Select a gene to remove. Blank imprint + catalyst: 10 s. Edits culture in place and returns its gene imprint. Costs 1 biomass and 25 stability; dependent genes prevent removal.
jei.bioforge.splicer.recover: Nutrient medium: 10 s, restores 1 biomass (max 3) and 25 stability (max 100). Genes remain intact. Example culture starts at 1 biomass / 60 stability.
gui.bioforge.splicer.examine_help: Study this category in 5 seconds. Mutations: Surfactant Concentrate. Transmissions: Catalyst Vial. Symptoms: Nutrient Medium. One reagent per category; editing the genome requires fresh analysis and study.
jei.bioforge.splicer.study_mutation: Study mutations: Surfactant Concentrate, 5 s. Unlocks mutation viewing, extraction and editing until the genome changes.
jei.bioforge.splicer.study_transmission: Study transmissions: Catalyst Vial, 5 s. Unlocks transmission viewing, extraction and editing until the genome changes.
jei.bioforge.splicer.study_symptom: Study symptoms: Nutrient Medium, 5 s. Unlocks symptom viewing, extraction and editing until the genome changes.
item.bioforge.hazmat.dye_hint: Dye on a crafting table; mix dyes. Wash color off in a water cauldron.
research.bioforge.page.field_medicine_qu: Craft a Herbal Mortar from cobblestone, a bowl and a stick. Sugar + paper + a plant makes four ready-to-use tablets in 8 seconds. The tablet page lists all four plants.

Craft four Swabs from wool and a stick; sterilizing water is unnecessary. Sample an infected host. A Field Vaccine Maker needs the infected sample, an empty field dose and sugar. No gene sequence or settings: wait 40 seconds.

Sugar gives 10% quality, glistering melon 25%. Quality is not cure chance. Field doses use 15% or 25% of normal calculated potency, with cure chance capped at 15% or 25%. Both share a 60-second cooldown, including diffuser attempts on the same patient. Partial protection lasts five minutes; Vaccine Maker creates stronger vaccines.
research.bioforge.page.symptom_tablets.c: Always use sugar and paper. Add dried kelp for coughing, poppy for sneezing, dandelion for fever, or beetroot for nausea. Each batch gives four tablets after 8 seconds.

Tablets suppress a specific symptom temporarily; they do not remove the pathogen or its transmission genes. High infection strength and analgesic resistance shorten relief. Loss of coughing is not proof of recovery.

Take tablets directly, use them on a patient, or put them in a Medical Diffuser. One tablet powers three minutes of mist and is consumed once at startup, even in an empty room. The mist attempts symptom relief every second for everyone in the connected room.
research.bioforge.page.medical_diffuser_: Insert a filled full vaccine and a water bucket. One vaccine dose powers the whole two-minute cycle with repeated treatment attempts; no vaccine-defense mutations are created. The empty bucket returns to the output.

One ready or programmed tablet is consumed once and powers three minutes of spraying. Attempts repeat every second for all biological hosts in the connected room, even without symptoms or patients. Another tablet waits in the input until this dose finishes. The active programmed profile and remaining time survive reload.

Redstone pauses medicine and water timers. Tablets suspend the remaining vaccine cycle and it resumes afterwards. If water runs out, refill the water slot: the active dose stays saved and does not cost another tablet. Directed vaccines and mutagens are not accepted.
Crafting requires a microscope, which becomes part of Gene Splicer. Gene Splicer is a separate block. Insert an infected Swab, blood sample, culture vial or Petri Dish. Clean blood has no pathogen genes. Analysis takes 30 seconds, or 10 with CRISPR notes matching this strain.

Optional notes matching this strain reduce analysis from 30 to 10 seconds. Select a category, put its study reagent in the Reagent slot and press Study. The category page lists the three reagents. A blank Gene Imprint extracts the selected identified gene. For insertion, use an identified compatible imprint and Catalyst Vial; study the imprint category first.

Vaccine Maker no longer extracts genes. Insert and Remove edit the sample in its slot, including Live Culture Vials, and require fresh analysis and study afterwards. Put a filled Live Culture Vial alone in the crafting grid to convert it to a Virus Sample, preserving its genes and reserves. Clear the splicer output before operating.
research.bioforge.page.splicer_gene_cate: Study takes 5 seconds and consumes one reagent: mutations use Surfactant Concentrate, transmissions use Catalyst Vial, symptoms use Nutrient Medium. Study unlocks viewing, extraction and editing for that category until the genome changes.

Culture starts with 3 biomass and 100 stability. Extract: 6 seconds, 1 biomass and 10 stability, minimum stability 30. Insert or Remove: 10 seconds, 1 biomass and 25 stability, minimum stability 60, plus one Catalyst Vial.

Nutrient Medium in the Food slot restores 1 biomass and 25 stability in 10 seconds. A depleted culture stays intact. Moving it cannot reset reserves. Mutation prerequisites and conflicts are checked; deleting a mutation does not automatically undo its symptom or transmission genes.

research.bioforge.page.foodborne_risks.c: Raw beef, pork, chicken, mutton, rabbit, cod and salmon have a 5% chance per meal to carry a mild parasite. It immediately causes Hunger I for 60 seconds, then the infection and its hunger clear automatically. Cooked foods have no natural food risk by default.

Rotten flesh instead has a separate 2% prion risk. Incubation lasts 30 seconds; the active infection lasts five minutes and can cause nausea from neural damage. Its vanilla hunger chance still applies separately. Existing infections are not replaced by these natural risks.
Choose cooked meat and avoid rotten flesh. Symptom tablets can ease discomfort, but they do not remove the parasite or prion. Identify the pathogen before selecting a treatment.
research.bioforge.page.rabies_guide.cont: Newly spawned wolves, cats, foxes, ocelots and bats have a 0.01% chance (one in ten thousand) to carry rabies. It spreads through bites and has a four-minute natural incubation.

Rabid Aggression makes both passive and hostile biological mobs attack players and creatures, including infected creatures and other rabid hosts. Armor stands, nonbiological entities, creative and spectator players remain excluded. Curing the infection restores normal behavior.

Original Zombie Neurotropism makes passive hosts attack survival players regardless of infection and uninfected mobs, sparing infected mobs. Rabies also targets infected mobs. Both mutations can be studied with Gene Splicer.
mutation.bioforge.rabid_aggression.name: Rabid Aggression
mutation.bioforge.rabid_aggression.descr: After incubation, the host attacks healthy and infected creatures alike. Curing restores normal behavior.

research.bioforge.tablet_navigation.body:
Search: type a name, item ID or words from the page. Select a section above the search field; clear the search to see all pages in that section.

Navigation: < and > revisit pages. H opens the contents. Click an underlined link to open its protocol.

Bookmarks: press * to save a page. The gold button marks a saved page; find it in Bookmarks.

Scroll the page text and recipe area separately. Hover an item for its full name. Locked pages show their names; obtain the required item to unlock their contents.
research.bioforge.page.personal_vitals.c: Players can have different healthy temperatures, heartbeat rhythms, oxygen saturation and perfusion. A higher temperature or faster heartbeat can be normal for that patient.
A fever raises temperature by 1.9 C above the patient's own normal; cold lowers it by 1.1 C. Compare readings with that patient's normal rather than another player.
Medical records retain the disease-related changes separately. Vaccine Maker uses these changes, so a personal normal does not count as an infection symptom.
item.bioforge.stethoscope.tooltip.site: Shift + right-click switches between heart and lungs.

command.bioforge.physiology.invalid_hear: Heart rhythm must be NORMAL, TACHY or BRADY.
research.bioforge.page.auscultation.cont: The stethoscope has two modes: Heart and Lungs. Shift + right-click switches them. Hold right-click to listen to yourself or the creature you are looking at.
Heart mode shows and plays the heartbeat. Lungs mode shows and plays breathing. Only the selected organ is examined.
Record heart and lungs separately for a complete examination. Switching modes does not change the patient or infection.
Some active infections can cause brief heartbeat-in-ears or scratching sounds. Personal audio settings can mute them, voices, coughing or sneezing.
research.bioforge.page.animal_infections: Animals can carry different bacterial, viral, fungal and parasitic strains. Most newly encountered animals are healthy. Each animal is checked once; reloading a chunk or curing it does not roll another natural infection.

Take a blood sample or swab, identify the pathogen and inspect its genes before choosing a vaccine. Separate sick animals; cook meat and use clean water. Filters help against airborne strains, but contact, food and water require their own precautions.

Pigs and hoglins: 5%, respiratory virus or intestinal parasite. Cows and mooshrooms: 4%, enteric bacteria, intestinal parasite or skin fungus. Chickens and parrots: 6%, surface virus or enteric bacteria. These percentages are the total chance of infection, not a separate roll for each disease.

Sheep and goats: 3.5%, intestinal parasites or skin fungus. Horses, donkeys, mules, llamas and camels: 2.5%, intestinal parasites or a mild respiratory virus. Rabbits: 3%, enteric bacteria or intestinal parasites.

Wolves and cats: 1.5%, contact bacteria or intestinal parasites. Foxes, ocelots, pandas and polar bears: 2%, contact or intestinal infections. Bats: 2%, a mild respiratory virus or intestinal parasites. Bees: 2%, a surface fungus or contact bacteria.

Ordinary infections do not make these animals aggressive. Rabies remains a separate very rare possibility for wolves, cats, foxes, ocelots and bats: its rule has a 0.01% chance. Keep newly encountered animals apart until examined.

Cod, salmon, tropical fish and pufferfish: 3%, waterborne bacteria or aquatic parasites. Dolphins and turtles: 2%, the same two disease families. Frogs and axolotls: 3%, a skin fungus or aquatic parasites.

Waterborne and foodborne strains need clean water and properly prepared food; an air filter alone cannot protect against them. The new ordinary animal strains have an incubation period and reduced infectivity. Study a sample before treatment; suppressing symptoms alone does not remove the pathogen.
jei.bioforge.incubator.operation.convert: Converts Living Bottle to Virus Sample; preserves the complete culture
gui.bioforge.splicer.genome_hint: Only genes stored in this sample are listed. Symptoms include stored normal values. Coughing and sneezing are in Mutations.
research.bioforge.incubator.conversion: Put an infected Living Bottle in the upper Incubator slot and Nutrient Medium in a lower slot. After 10 seconds, one bottle and one medium become one Virus Sample. The genome and culture reserves are preserved.
research.bioforge.page.symptom_reference: For hypothermia, stay within about 3 blocks of lit campfires, working furnaces, smokers, blast furnaces, lava or fire; being on fire also provides warmth. For fever, enter water or stand on ice. Appropriate warmth or cooling completely prevents damage from the corresponding temperature symptom. It does not cure the infection or prevent ordinary fire and lava damage.
research.bioforge.page.minecraft_infecti: Sculk infection: 25% of Wardens carry a fungal strain spread through contact and contaminated surfaces. It causes chills and slowed reflexes. Its Sculk Echo gene causes persistent blindness: creature sounds reveal the surrounding surfaces as cyan echo waves. Sound rays reflect off blocks; wool absorbs reflections. Silence leaves the world dark.

End flu: carried by 4% of Endermen, 8% of Shulkers and 10% of Endermites. Air and contact spread a virus causing fever, coughing and nausea. Its Ender Displacement gene attempts a safe random teleport within ten blocks every five minutes; it skips the attempt if no safe destination is found.

Wither blight: 12% of Wither Skeletons carry a bacterial strain spread by attacks and contact. Tissue damage, weakness and short bouts of Wither distinguish it from ordinary fever. The undead carrier may resist its own symptoms.

These are occasional carriers, not guaranteed infections. Incubation gives time to isolate a sample; the strains have finite active lifetimes and moderate infectivity. Use blood or a swab for research, extract their special genes in the Gene Splicer, and prepare a matching vaccine. Symptom tablets provide temporary relief.
mutation.bioforge.sculk_resonance.name: Sculk Resonance
mutation.bioforge.sculk_resonance.descri: Neural sculk growth causes brief slowdowns and soul-like motes.
mutation.bioforge.ender_disorientation.d: Brief bouts of nausea and portal-like motes. Brief spatial distortions leave movement trails.
mutation.bioforge.wither_necrosis.name: Wither Necrosis
mutation.bioforge.wither_necrosis.descri: Intermittent weakness and short bouts of Wither. Vision loses color and develops dark veins around its edges.
mutation.bioforge.ender_displacement.des: Attempts a safe random teleport within ten blocks every five minutes.
mutation.bioforge.sculk_echo.name: Sculk Echo
mutation.bioforge.sculk_echo.description: Persistent blindness replaces sight with sound-driven echo waves reflected by blocks. Occasional false echoes can mislead the listener.
research.bioforge.page.sensory_disturban: Paranoia can show eyes, faces or silhouettes in dark peripheral areas. Looking directly at an apparition, approaching it or bringing light makes it disappear. These hallucinations do not create real creatures.

Sculk Echo can occasionally produce a false sound source and reflected waves. Ender Disorientation causes brief spatial distortions and movement trails. Wither Necrosis drains color and draws dark veins around the edges of your vision.

Low blood oxygen narrows vision and makes its edges pulse with your heart rate. These additional visual symptoms begin after incubation and stop when the infection is cured or the responsible gene is removed.
In bioforge-client.toml, [visuals] lets you disable each additional effect or adjust intensity. The sculk echo sound has a separate switch under [audio.symptoms].
